title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes Grothendieck works with an abstract combinatorial model of 'figures', apparently meant to support a tame or stratified topology. There is a set M of 'objects', which can be thought of as cells or strata. M is ordered and carries the associated (Alexandrov-type) topology. A family 𝓕 of 'figures' F, each a subset or sup of objects, is subject to axioms C1, C2, C3. M_{≤F} is the set of objects contained in F, and \bar F is the corresponding open set of M.

The previous page proved that a subfigure F_0 ⊂ F is a connected component of F iff \bar F_0 is a connected component of the open set A = \bar F ⊂ M. Page 63 completes this. It gives a bijection between the connected components of F and those of A. It also states that F is the disjoint direct sum of its components, F = Sup_i F_i with the F_i pairwise disjoint.

New section, 'connected components of the ambient structure'. Write M = ∐_{i∈I} M_i for the decomposition of M into connected components, I = π_0(M).
- For a figure F set F_i = Sup{X ∈ M_i ∩ M_{≤F}}. A marginal note seems to describe F_i as the largest subfigure of F contained in M_i.
- Then F is the direct sum of the F_i. A marginal remark is added, roughly '(case / since I = π_0(M) finite!)'. This shows awareness that infinite sups are problematic.
- If F is 'de t.f.' (finite type), all but finitely many F_i are empty.
- Let 𝓕_i = {F ∈ 𝓕 : F ⊂ M_i}. Then 𝓕_i satisfies C1, C2, and C3 if 𝓕 does, and M_i is one of its indecomposable objects.
- For F ∈ 𝓕 we have F_i = F ∩ M_i and F = ∐ F_i, a disjoint union.
- For fixed i, the projection 𝓕 → 𝓕_i commutes with finite sups and with nonempty infs.
- The map 𝓕 → ∏ 𝓕_i, F ↦ (F_i), is injective, and the order of 𝓕 is induced by the product order.

The next page asks for the image of this map. It introduces C4: objects lying in distinct components are compatible. With C4 the image is the restricted product (F_i = ∅ for almost all i). The map is a bijection when I is finite.

In modern terms: the lattice of 'closed/finite' subobjects of a space (or of a poset with Alexandrov topology, or of a stratified space) decomposes along π_0 as a restricted product of the lattices of the components. This is the lattice-theoretic form of 'a space is the coproduct of its connected components'.
errors: The claim that F is the direct sum of the F_i requires the sup to exist. Grothendieck himself flags this: in the marginal '(car/cas I = π_0(M) fini!)', and on p. 64 via the C4 condition and finite-type hypotheses. As written on p. 63 the statement is only justified for I finite or F of finite type.
The claim that 𝓕_i satisfies C1–C3 is asserted without proof. The axioms are not visible on this page, so the check cannot be completed here.

ideas.what: Bijection between connected components of a figure F and connected components of the associated open set \bar F ⊂ M; F is the disjoint sum of its components.
ideas.modern_name: Connected components of a subcomplex / open set in an Alexandrov (poset) space; decomposition into components
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Alexandrov 1937 for poset topologies; standard algebraic topology)

ideas.what: Decomposition of the lattice of figures along π_0(M): 𝓕 ↪ ∏ 𝓕_i, order induced by the product, projections commuting with finite sups and nonempty infs; restricted product under C4.
ideas.modern_name: Decomposition of a lattice / frame of subobjects over connected components (restricted product of lattices); coproduct decomposition of a space
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore in lattice theory and topology

deep.surprise_reason: This is careful but routine bookkeeping: connected components and the product decomposition of the lattice of figures, inside an axiomatic framework for 'analysis situs'. The framework itself (C1–C4 for figures) is of some historical interest as part of Grothendieck's unpublished tame-topology project. This page contains no new result or connection.
transcription_corrections: Line after the definition of F_i: should read roughly 'Si F est de t.f., alors tous les F_i sauf un nb fini sont ∅' (all but finitely many F_i are empty). It does not read 'Si F est de la forme 𝒥'.
The left-margin note near the definition of F_i appears to read 'F_i la plus grande sous-figure de F contenue dans M_i' (or similar).
The marginal parenthesis reads '(car' or '(cas I = π_0(M) fini!)'. 'cas' is plausible, which would make it a case restriction rather than an assertion.
The section heading's second part is hard to read ('𝔈le cont. F'?). 'l'ensemble contrôlé' is conjectural.
The top-left marginal note reads approximately 'NB Dans ... besoin de C3'. It is a remark on where axiom C3 is needed.
